store.tagline: Start, stop and restart systemd units and launchd jobs
features: Linux: every systemd unit, user and system, filtered by User, System, Failed or Running, its state in colour
`enter` starts or stops a unit; system units ask first and use sudo or pkexec as allowed
`cmd+l` shows the unit's recent log, `cmd+e` enables or disables it
macOS: your launch agents and every loaded job, tagged running, loaded, exited or not loaded
`enter` loads or unloads a job after a confirm, `cmd+shift+r` restarts it, `cmd+l` shows its plist

screenshots.caption: systemd units under the User filter: whether each is enabled, and whether it is running, idle or failed
The Failed filter gathers what broke across both managers, in a User and a System section
cmd+l shows a unit's journal in the panel: why last night's backup failed
On macOS, launchd agents by folder, with their pid and state
A unit's detail (cmd+I): its manager and file, the name, failed and enabled as chips, what it is for

actions.title: Stop
actions.description: systemctl stop on an active unit; a system unit asks first.

actions.title: Start
actions.description: systemctl start on an inactive unit.

actions.title: Restart
actions.description: systemctl restart, or launchctl kickstart -k on macOS.

actions.title: Enable
actions.description: systemctl enable on a disabled unit file.

actions.title: Disable
actions.description: systemctl disable; a system unit asks first.

actions.title: Load
actions.description: macOS: launchctl bootstrap from the plist.

actions.title: Show plist
actions.description: macOS: the plist as XML in the panel.
